import re
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path


DEFAULT_REPORT_PATH = Path("docs/q3_report.md")
DEFAULT_NOTES_PATH = Path("docs/meeting_notes_2026_09.txt")

INSERTION_MARKER = "[[INSERT_Q3_2026_REPORT_HERE]]"
START_MARKER = "----- BEGIN Q3 2026 BUSINESS REPORT -----"
END_MARKER = "----- END Q3 2026 BUSINESS REPORT -----"

REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTIONS = ("Rachel Kim", "Claire Fontaine")

TARGET_DATE_PATTERNS = (
    r"(?im)^(?:#+\s*)?September\s+8,\s+2026\b.*$",
    r"(?im)^(?:#+\s*)?Sep(?:tember)?\.?\s+8,\s+2026\b.*$",
    r"(?im)^(?:#+\s*)?2026[-/]09[-/]08\b.*$",
)

# Recognizes date-like headings so the script can determine where the
# September 8 section ends. Add another format here if your notes use one.
ANY_DATE_HEADING_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"""(?imx)^
        (?:\#{1,6}[ \t]*)?
        (?:
            (?:Jan(?:uary)?|Feb(?:ruary)?|Mar(?:ch)?|Apr(?:il)?|May|
               Jun(?:e)?|Jul(?:y)?|Aug(?:ust)?|Sep(?:tember)?|
               Oct(?:ober)?|Nov(?:ember)?|Dec(?:ember)?)
            \.?[ \t]+\d{1,2},?[ \t]+\d{4}
          |
            \d{4}[-/]\d{1,2}[-/]\d{1,2}

        \b[^\r\n]*$

    raise RuntimeError(message)

    """Use the destination file's existing newline style."""
    crlf = raw.count(b"\r\n")
    lf = raw.count(b"\n") - crlf
    cr = raw.count(b"\r") - crlf

    if crlf >= lf and crlf >= cr and crlf:
        return b"\r\n"
    if cr > lf and cr:
        return b"\r"
    return b"\n"

    try:

    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        fail(f"{label} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}")

    """
    Locate exactly one September 8 heading.

    Matches are deduplicated because more than one accepted regex can match
    the same heading.
    """
    matches_by_span: dict[tuple[int, int], re.Match[str]] = {}

    for pattern in TARGET_DATE_PATTERNS:
        for match in re.finditer(pattern, notes_text):
            matches_by_span[(match.start(), match.end())] = match

    matches = list(matches_by_span.values())

    heading through the character before the next recognized date heading.
